observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: Two stack arguments, both read after the pushes: 0x00ba61da MOV ESI,[ESP + 0xC] with ESP = entry-4 reads [E+8], the SECOND argument, and 0x00ba61df MOV EDI,[ESP + 0xC] with ESP = entry-8 reads [E+4], the FIRST argument. The epilogue is a bare RET at 0x00ba6223 after ADD ESP,0xC / POP EDI / POP ESI, and the ADD ESP,0xC discards exactly the two words pushed for 0x006AC040 and 0x006AD010 plus the earlier PUSH EDI. So the CALLER owns all stack cleanup. This is __cdecl, not __thiscall: ECX is used only as the receiver of 0x00B8E180, 0x00B8DA80 and the slot +0x00 virtual, never as an incoming parameter.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: No return value. The constructed object is delivered through the second argument, an out-parameter.

stack_arguments.use: written to the object's +0x08, passed to 0x00B8DA80 which stores it at +0x184, and passed to the slot +0x00 virtual through the pushed register
the out-pointer. Stored to at 0x00ba61e6 and then RELOADED from at 0x00ba61ed, 0x00ba6204 and 0x00ba620c rather than kept in a register.

observed_original_abi.hidden_receiver: none. This is a factory, not a member function. ECX is a scratch register reused as the receiver of three successive calls.
observed_original_abi.hidden_this_register: ECX is never read on entry. It is loaded at 0x00ba61ce with the allocated block for the constructor, at 0x00ba61e4 with the same block for the setter, and at 0x00ba6204 for the slot +0x00 virtual. No incoming register carries a receiver.
observed_original_abi.out_parameter_reload_note: The out-pointer is re-read from memory three times after being written. The reconstruction preserves this by re-reading the caller's pointer rather than caching the object, because the reloads are what the original does and a callee that wrote through the out-pointer would be observed.

layout.padding_after: not read; the body ends at the bare RET 0x00ba6223.
layout.frame: No SUB ESP and no EBP frame. Two registers are saved with PUSH ESI / PUSH EDI after the allocator call, and the ADD ESP,0xC / POP EDI / POP ESI epilogue is balanced because the two inner cdecl calls each left one word behind.
layout.reads: the two caller stack arguments; nothing else is read from the receiver, because the receiver is the freshly allocated object and every field write goes through the out-pointer.
layout.writes: three dwords of the object's header, at +0x08, +0x0C and +0x10, plus whatever 0x00B8E180 and 0x00B8DA80 write, plus one dword through the caller's out-pointer. Five direct calls.

observed_mechanics: 0x00ba61b0..0x00ba61b6: four PUSH 0. 0x00ba61b8 PUSH 0x01465EF0. 0x00ba61bd PUSH 0x1B0. The allocation is 0x1B0 = 432 bytes with a type descriptor at 0x01465EF0.
0x00ba61c2 CALL 0x00F473A0 / 0x00ba61c7 ADD ESP,0x18: the allocator is cdecl with six stack arguments, cleaned by the caller.
0x00ba61ca TEST EAX,EAX / 0x00ba61cc JZ 0x00ba61d7: on failure 0x00ba61d7 XOR EAX,EAX supplies a null object and the constructor is skipped.
0x00ba61ce MOV ECX,EAX / 0x00ba61d0 CALL 0x00B8E180: the 459-byte constructor, called with no stack argument because it ends in a bare RET.

0x00ba61d9 PUSH ESI / 0x00ba61da MOV ESI,[ESP + 0xC]: with ESP = entry-4 this reads [E+8], the out-pointer. 0x00ba61de PUSH EDI / 0x00ba61df MOV EDI,[ESP + 0xC]: with ESP = entry-8 this reads [E+4], the planet id.
0x00ba61e3 PUSH EDI / 0x00ba61e4 MOV ECX,EAX / 0x00ba61e6 MOV [ESI],EAX: the out-pointer is written BEFORE the setter runs, and 0x00ba61e8 CALL 0x00B8DA80 ends in RET 4 so it pops the pushed id.
0x00ba61ed MOV EAX,[ESI] / 0x00ba61ef ADD EAX,0x8: the object is reloaded from the out-pointer and biased by 8, so the three header writes are at +0x08, +0x0C and +0x10.

0x00ba61f4 MOV ECX,0x5220CB8 / 0x00ba61f9 MOV [EAX + 0x4],ECX: the constant 0x5220CB8 at +0x0C. This worker resolves it to NOTHING. It is read as an immediate and is not claimed to be a property id, a type hash, a class id or anything else.
0x00ba61fc MOV EDX,0x1 / 0x00ba6201 MOV [EAX + 0x8],EDX: the value 1 at +0x10.

0x00ba6204 MOV ECX,[ESI] / 0x00ba6206 MOV EAX,[ECX] / 0x00ba6208 MOV EDX,[EAX] / 0x00ba620a CALL EDX: virtual call at vtable slot +0x00 with ECX = the object and NO stack arguments. Nothing is pushed before it and nothing is popped after it.
0x00ba620c MOV EAX,[ESI] / 0x00ba620e PUSH EAX / 0x00ba620f PUSH 0x1 / 0x00ba6211 CALL 0x006AC040: cdecl two-argument call, the words left for the epilogue's ADD ESP,0xC.
0x00ba6216 MOV ECX,[ESI] / 0x00ba6218 PUSH ECX / 0x00ba6219 CALL 0x006AD010: cdecl one-argument call.

0x00ba621e ADD ESP,0xC / 0x00ba6221 POP EDI / 0x00ba6222 POP ESI / 0x00ba6223 RET: the ADD discards the two words from 0x006AD010 and 0x006AC040 plus the PUSH EDI from 0x00ba61e3, leaving the two saved registers to be popped and a bare RET.

The type-name string passed at 0x00ba61b8 is at the address held in 0x01465EF0. Read live, the corresponding literal in the neighbouring region of .rdata is "Simulator/cPlanetRecord". That literal is what establishes the owning class; it is not the immediate 0x01465EF0 itself, which this worker did not dereference independently of the decompiler's own rendering of the allocator call.

There is NO null check on the out-pointer. If the allocation fails, 0x00ba61ed reads 0, 0x00ba61ef makes it 8, and 0x00ba61f2 writes the planet id to absolute address 8. The reconstruction reproduces that unchecked write rather than inventing a guard.

sdk_correspondence.caveat: Spore-ModAPI is a third-party clean-room reconstruction, not original EA source and not EA documentation. Where it is cited below it supplies CANDIDATE NAMES only. The binary is the sole authority for every offset, constant, branch polarity and call shape asserted in this record.

semantic_contract: A cdecl factory that allocates a 0x1B0-byte object named "Simulator/cPlanetRecord", constructs it, sets its planet-id field at +0x184 through the setter 0x00B8DA80, writes a three-dword header at +0x08 (the planet id), +0x0C (the constant 0x5220CB8) and +0x10 (the value 1), calls vtable slot +0x00 on the new object with no arguments, then calls 0x006AC040(record, 1) and 0x006AD010(record), and delivers the object through the caller's second argument. The out-pointer is written before the setter runs and is then reloaded from memory three times rather than cached in a register. The function pops nothing: the caller owns the two stack words. There is no null check on the out-pointer, so an allocation failure writes to absolute address 8; that fault is reproduced rather than repaired.
classification_rationale: Not STRONG_SEMANTIC. The complete 116-byte body, the cdecl ABI including the exact stack cleanup, all five call sites, the vtable slot +0x00, every constant and all three header writes are read directly from the disassembly, and the owning class is established by a type-name literal rather than guessed. But the material elements that are bounded rather than established are numerous and central: the constructor at 0x00B8E180 was located but not reconstructed, so the vtable the slot +0x00 call goes through is unknown; the constant 0x5220CB8 is not resolved to anything; and the two engine-boundary calls 0x006AC040 and 0x006AD010 are opaque. Not STRUCTURAL_ONLY, because the allocation size, the type name, the header triple, the call order and the crash-on-alloc-failure behaviour are all established.
semantic_findings: This is a factory, not a member function: __cdecl, two stack arguments, no incoming receiver, bare RET. ECX is a scratch register reused for three successive callees.
The allocation is 0x1B0 bytes with the type name "Simulator/cPlanetRecord", which is the only literal type name located in this whole batch.

The object is delivered through the caller's out-pointer, which is written at 0x00ba61e6 BEFORE the setter runs and then RELOADED from memory at 0x00ba61ed, 0x00ba6204 and 0x00ba620c rather than cached in a register.
The planet id is written TWICE: once to +0x08 directly and once to +0x184 through 0x00B8DA80. The two writes carry the same value.
0x5220CB8 is stored at +0x0C and is not resolved to any property, type, class or enum name by this worker. It is recorded as a bare observed constant.
vtable slot +0x00 is called with NO stack arguments on the freshly constructed object, so the callee pops nothing.

The allocation-failure path is a genuine fault in the original: the null is stored through the out-pointer and then dereferenced at +8. Reproduced, not repaired, and deliberately not exercised by the model test.

The epilogue's ADD ESP,0xC is balanced by three words that are still on the stack at that point: the PUSH EDI from 0x00ba61e3 and the two words the cdecl 0x006AC040 and 0x006AD010 calls each left behind. The stack discipline is exact and was confirmed against the callees' ret forms.
unresolved_questions: What is 0x5220CB8? It is read as an immediate at 0x00ba61f4 and stored at +0x0C. No name, type, key or hash is claimed for it.
What is at +0x10, set to 1? A count, a flag, a reference count and a version are all consistent with the single observed write.
Which class does vtable slot +0x00 belong to? The table address is written by the constructor 0x00B8E180, whose body was not reconstructed, so the concrete callee is unresolved.
What do 0x006AC040(record, 1) and 0x006AD010(record) do? Both are engine-boundary calls, 82 and 28 instructions, neither characterised.

What is 0x01465EF0? It is the type descriptor passed to the allocator. The decompiler renders the allocator's second argument as the literal "Simulator/cPlanetRecord" and the corresponding bytes are present in .rdata, but this worker did not follow the pointer 0x01465EF0 to its target, so the association is strong rather than byte-traced end to end.

What does the 459-byte constructor 0x00B8E180 initialise? It was located and its ret form read, but its body was not reconstructed, so no field claim is made beyond the first dword being the vtable pointer.
What is the calling convention of the six callers' own sites? None of the six callers was disassembled, so the argument order at each callsite is unverified even though the callee's own reads fix it.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists. A differential run must confirm the allocation size 0x1B0, the type name and the three header writes in the shipping build.
The 0x5220CB8 constant can only be attributed by observing what reads +0x0C on a constructed record at runtime.
The crash-on-allocation-failure path can only be confirmed as intentional or as a latent defect by forcing an allocation failure in a controlled run.
The concrete callee behind vtable slot +0x00 can only be fixed by dumping the vtable pointer of a constructed record.
